Stat.ModTooltip: Ancestry and age included. The value entered is an adult's (16 and over).

Settings.ForceHouseHint: Override this sheet's house color (blank = use actor's house)

Animagus.Title: Animagus

Profile.brave: Brave, heroic, headstrong — lion, bear, stag, horse…
Profile.loyal: Loyal and unfailingly devoted — dog, wolf, badger…
Profile.playful: Playful, mischievous and vengeful — cat, otter, weasel, squirrel, magpie, fox…
Profile.solitary: Solitary, taking revenge slyly — snake, spider, bat, rat…
Profile.timid: Timid, retiring, good-natured — roe deer, doe, hedgehog, small rodents, rabbit…

Animagus.ProfileHint: Result of the §16.2 personality test, which gives the animal category. The questionnaire itself is not reproduced: refer to the book.
Animagus.MasteryHint: House extension: the book publishes no mastery tiers.
Animagus.TransformHint: House extension: roll against the Animagus skill. The book describes the process (§16.1) without any numbers.
Animagus.NoSkill: This character does not have the Animagus skill.

Character.AgeMalusHint: 2d6+6 gives an adult's value (16 and over). One point is removed from STR, CON and SIZ per missing year; the malus shrinks by one each year.
Character.StressHint: Stress malus applied to all rolls (0-25%)

NPC.YearBonusHint: §22.2.1: a character created in an advanced year gains skill points on top of the base budget. The ceiling used is the top of the book's range.
NPC.RivalHint: §21.2 advises building rivals as anti-heroes, created like player characters. When ticked, the NPC gets 400 skill points and 6 perk points instead of 350 and 4.5.
NPC.AffinityHint: A wand affinity grants +10% in one element or one type of spell (§21.1).
NPC.DamageHint: Default attack, used when the NPC carries no weapon.
NPC.Steps: §21.1 steps handled elsewhere: skills and characteristics in their own tabs, perks and house axiom under Perks. An NPC starts with one level 1 spell and one level 0 spell.

Skills.SpentExceeded: Cannot spend above remaining cap (max - base).

MaxAuto.Override: Set this maximum manually (stops the per-year progression)
MaxAuto.Restore: Back to the automatic per-year maximum
MaxAuto.RestoreConfirm: The maximum for "{skill}" is set manually to {manual}%. Switching back to automatic will reset it to {auto}%, derived from the school year, and your entry will be lost.
MaxAuto.RestoreConfirmSame: The maximum for "{skill}" is set manually. Switching back to automatic will make it follow the school year again — {auto}% today, more each year — and your setting will be lost.

Skills.BaseHint: House extension: the book publishes no table of base masteries; these values belong to this system.
Skills.MaxHint: House extension: the book publishes no table of maximum masteries; these values belong to this system.
Skills.FeatureBonus: Of which granted by an advantage or disadvantage:

preSchool.label: Instinctive Spell (Pre-school)
preSchool.hint: House extension: the POW × 3 roll does not appear in the book. Uncheck to use the school skill instead.

Potion.NoIngredients: No ingredients specified. Add ingredients to enable crafting tracking.
Potion.BrewPerfect: Perfect potion: the potion's variable effects are maximised (l. 12922).
Potion.BrewFumble: Disaster! An unexpected side effect occurs!

Effect.AttributeReferenceHint: Keys you can target with an Active Effect, shown with their current value. Use the copy button and paste the key into the effect's Attribute Key field.

XP.Title: Experience Resolution
XP.NoChecks: No skills are marked for experience.
XP.EffectHint: XP effect keys: xp.multiplier, xp.multiplier.{category}, xp.multiplier.skill.{name}, xp.bonus, xp.bonus.{category}, xp.bonus.skill.{name}
XP.AllTermsDone: All three terms of the year are already credited.
XP.TermHint: Credit the first week then each end of term (§7.3, §25.1)
XP.HolidayHint: 1d10+1% if the pupil goes home instead of playing (l. 28202)
XP.SpendHint: To be spread over non-school skills only. Remaining: {pool}%.
XP.Unlock: Unlock a lore or a language ({cost}%)

Learn.Title: Spell Learning
Learn.Critical: Mastery! The spell is learned without penalty.
Learn.Success: The spell is learned normally (penalty maintained).
Learn.Fail: Spell memorised but unexpected effects may occur.
Learn.Fumble: Psychological block! A teacher is required.

Assistance.Label: Assistance
Assistance.Hint: Support bonus from an ally (0 if none)

Roll.FougueChoice: The die shows {original}. Heroism can reverse it to {reversed}. The point is spent either way.

Chat.NotOwner: You do not control this character
Chat.FougueAtMax: The maximum of {max} Heroism points is already reached.

Creation.Title: Creation assistant
Creation.Intro: Eight {formula} rolls to spread across the characteristics, guided by the archetype. Picking a value already placed swaps it with the other characteristic.
Creation.AgeNote: At {age}, STR, CON and SIZ lose {malus} point(s). The malus shrinks by one each year until it is gone at 16.
Creation.Duplicate: One rolled value is used twice.

Derived.Title: Derived Characteristics
Derived.ThirdEyeHint: Magical sight granted by the "Third Eye" advantage: it adds to the other senses and is rolled under PERception × 4.

Settings.WarnOnNegativeExperienceHint: Show a notification when a spend would push an experience total below zero.
Settings.TabsUseIconsHint: When enabled, actor sheet tabs show FontAwesome icons instead of text labels (client preference).
Settings.UseExtendedTiersHint: Not an official rule: the book only defines a critical (01-05) and a fumble (96-00). The Extreme (≤ target/5) and Hard (≤ target/2) tiers are borrowed from generic BRP, rounded up, which no printed example in the source confirms. Off by default. Does not affect spell learning, for which the book prints exactly four outcomes.
Settings.ExcludeSchoolSkillsFromCPHint: When enabled, points spent in 'School Subjects' category skills are not counted toward the Creation Points total.
Settings.KnockoutMethodHint: Classic: resistance table opposition (§2.7.1). Alternative: 25/50/75% hit point loss thresholds (§2.7.2).
Settings.ApplyArmorOnDamageHint: Automatically applies the reduction of worn armour (§2.8.1).
Settings.RerollInitiativeHint: Per §2.2: every participant rolls 1d6+DEX again at the start of each round.
Settings.SchoolXpModeHint: The book publishes two contradictory versions. §25.1 (l. 28186) gives a flat 1d6+1 per term; §7.3 (l. 6848) a table tapering off with the subject's seniority.
Settings.FougueFailureIsFumbleHint: A roll missed after spending a Heroism point counts as a fumble (l. 2995). §8.3 frames it as a worst case rather than a certainty: uncheck to leave it a plain failure.
Settings.FougueAfterRollHint: The book spends the point BEFORE the roll (l. 10199). Uncheck to remove the chat-card button and allow only the roll-dialog checkbox.

Notifications.PersonalBonusNegative: Warning: Personal Bonus Points are negative

Spells.MaxMalus: Maximum penalty for learning spells from higher years

HousePoints.Title: House points
HousePoints.Hint: Click an action to roll 1d100 and determine the teacher's mood (§24.2).
HousePoints.ResetConfirm: Reset all four houses to zero?

loss.BookOutside: Taking a schoolbook outside the grounds

gain.MasterSpellPotion: Mastering a spell / potion in class
gain.WinDuel: Winning a wizard duel in class
gain.HelpStudent: Helping a student master a spell / potion

Opposition.TieRule: Tie: the action goes to whoever acts first in initiative order (l. 29822).
Opposition.NeedTwoMargins: At least two margins must be posted in chat.
Opposition.RollHint: Opposed roll: posts the margin instead of a success level (§28.3.4).

Duel.Title: Wizard duel

Type.a: a — First spell to take effect
Type.b: b — Put the opponent out of the fight

Step.challenge: The challenge is issued and accepted by every participant
Step.referee: Choose the referee who will declare the winner
Step.seconds: Each wizard picks a witness, who also stands in as their second
Step.declaration: Pick a spell and declare intent
Step.initiative: Roll initiative, then resolve in the resulting order

Duel.NoCombat: Open an encounter first: the duel rides on the combat tracker.
Duel.SpellNotOwned: This spell is not on the sheet: the target number must be entered by hand.
Duel.NoExtremeFormula: This spell has no extreme formula (the book prints “Formule extrême : -”): the normal malus applies.
Duel.DamageDisqualifies: In this duel type, 1 point of damage means immediate disqualification (§27.4).
Duel.WarnStar: The book stars this spell: it can wound or kill in some cases.
Duel.UnlinkedHint: This name appears in the duel table but matches no spell in the rulebook nor in the Grimoire.
Duel.PriorityHint: Resolution order: 1 innate, 2 protection, 3 unspoken and classic, 4 extreme formulas (§27.3).
Duel.ClubYearsHint: +1 duel initiative per year, up to +5, cumulative with the “Initié au duel” advantage (l. 28569).
Duel.Bow: The duellists face each other and bow, then take their fighting stance.
Duel.FouguePrompt: Spend a Fougue point to reroll the d6 with a +2 bonus? You do not yet know in which order your opponents will act (l. 28683).
Duel.FougueSpent: Fougue point spent: d6 rerolled with +2.

Mind.Title: Legilimency and Occlumency
Mind.MissingSkill: This character does not have the {skill} skill.
Mind.NoDefender: No actor has the Occlumancie skill.
Mind.ProximityHint: Physical proximity and eye contact make the intrusion easier; a calm and wary target makes it harder (§15.1). Translate that into a modifier.
Mind.Reversed: The intrusion turns back on the Legilimens
Mind.ReversalNote: {defender} blocks the spell as it is cast and enters {attacker}'s thoughts, who cannot shield themselves (§15.1, l. 24365). House extension: the book puts no numbers on this rule.

Quidditch.Title: Quidditch
Quidditch.NoCombat: Open an encounter first: the match rides on the combat tracker.
Quidditch.CoinToss: Coin toss: team {side} starts with the quaffle.
Quidditch.NoPlayers: No player assigned to this side.
Quidditch.NoAmount: Enter a number of points first.
Quidditch.ResetScoreConfirm: Reset the score to 0 — 0? The line-up and the snitch state are kept.
Quidditch.PenaltyRule: The chaser shoots from the centre circle; only the opposing keeper defends (l. 29542).

Snitch.Title: Golden snitch
Snitch.Spotted: The snitch is spotted: the chase starts at 30 metres.
Snitch.InReach: The snitch is in reach: a DEX x1 roll catches it.

Team.Label: Quidditch team
Team.Name: Team name
Team.DropHint: Drop a character on the sheet to add them to the roster.
Team.OnlyCharacters: Only characters can join a team.
Team.CaptainHint: Set as captain — only the captain may call a time-out (l. 29537).
Team.LineupOk: Regulation line-up: 3 chasers, 2 beaters, 1 keeper, 1 seeker.

Wound.Death: Reduced to 0 hit points: instant death (§1.8.3).
Wound.Staggered: Staggered: can only take a few steps this round (§1.10.2).
Wound.SaveSuccess: Success: the character shrugs off the shock.
Wound.KnockoutClassic: Resistance table: {dealt} damage against {hp} hit points → target {target}%, rolled {roll}.
Wound.KnockoutNoThreshold: Not enough damage to knock the target out.
Wound.KnockoutThirdDamage: On waking, the victim will only have taken 1/3 of the damage.

Recovery.Title: Weekly recovery
Recovery.CappedAtMax: Capped at the initial hit point total.

Reaction.Label: Reactions
Reaction.ParryHint: Parry — once per round, melee only (§2.5.2)
Reaction.DodgeNoAttack: A dodging character cannot attack this round.
Reaction.NotVsSpells: Spells can be neither parried nor dodged.
Reaction.AlreadyParried: Already parried this round: only one parry is allowed.
Reaction.NoParrySkill: No attacking skill available to parry with.

Capability.SpellEffectsThird: Spell effects cut to a third
Capability.SpellEffectsQuarter: Spell effects cut to a quarter

Errors.LinkSelf: An actor cannot be linked to itself.
Errors.LinkFamiliar: Only familiars can be linked to a character.

Fougue.EndScenarioConfirm: Reset every character's Heroism to 1 point, as at the start of a new scenario?
Fougue.SprintHint: Spend 1 Heroism point: movement +50% during a chase (§1.7.7).
Fougue.SprintResult: Running is limited to {rounds} round(s), followed by as many rounds of rest.
